newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of new U.S. military plan.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of new U.S. military plan.

text.p: Highlights of the Defence Department's quadrennial defence review, a new U.S. military security and forces proposal sent to Congress on Monday by Defence Secretary William Cohen:
- Asks for two new rounds of domestic military base closings in 1999 and 2001 to save money for new high-tech arms.
- Recommends minimal cut of 61,700 troops from 1.4 million-member active-duty armed forces. Air Force would lose 26,900, Navy 18,000, Army 15,000 and Marine Corps 1,800.
- Cuts National Guard and Reserves by 54,000, including 45,000 from Army, and eliminates 60,800 civilians employed by services.
- Retains current strategy of forward-deployed forces, including 100,000 in Europe and 100,000 in western Pacific, prepared to fight and win two wars at once.

- Outlines some reductions, but no cancellations, in Air Force F-22 "stealth" fighters being developed by Lockheed Martin Corp., Navy FA-18E/F fighters built by McDonnell Douglas Corp. and Marine Corps' V-22 tilt-rotor helicopters built by Boeing Co. and Textron Inc..
- Retains long-range plans for expected $170 billion joint strike fighter programme that Lockheed Martin and Boeing are competing to build in next century.
- Keeps 12 aircraft carriers in Navy and does not change Air Force's current plans to increase B-2 "stealth" bomber fleet to 21 aircraft.
